C1.statement: Superconducting: τ*_log < τ*_phys (empirical), with the learned decoder, in both bases. Trapped ion with crosstalk off: no idle-driven optimum. Trapped ion with crosstalk at the card value: an interior τ*_log < τ*_phys appears
C1.note: Superconducting (stage3_sc_dense.json, stage3_sc_x_dense.json; learned; against τ*_phys (empirical) = 0.910 µs): refuted. Interval below τ*_phys: X d3 soft 0.677 [0.599, 0.906] µs. Containing or above it: Z d3 hard 0.710 [0.662, 0.990] µs; Z d3 soft 0.694 [0.563, 0.912] µs; Z d5 hard 0.942 [0.643, 0.977] µs; Z d5 soft 0.844 [0.518, 0.983] µs; X d3 hard 0.696 [0.685, 0.946] µs; X d5 hard 0.653 [0.629, 1.01] µs; X d5 soft 0.900 [0.642, 1.01] µs. shiftDelta resolves no learned row. Trapped ion (crosstalkScan, learned), pre-registered point flag: crosstalk off refuted (flag at Z d3 hard, Z d3 soft); card rate undetermined (2 of 6 rows flagged); any rate held. Resolved flag (whole interval below τ*_phys, E12): off held, card rate refuted, any rate held (Z 0.001 /µs d3 hard, Z 0.001 /µs d3 soft, Z 0.001 /µs d5 hard, Z 0.001 /µs d5 soft, X 0.001 /µs d3 hard, X 0.001 /µs d3 soft). shiftDelta (E14): off held, card rate refuted, any rate held (X 0.001 /µs d3 hard, X 0.001 /µs d3 soft). Person A's reading of the ion parts uses the resolved flag (refuted), because the point flag reads noise in a flat minimum (E12 (a)). The overall verdict is refuted under either flag, because the superconducting part is.
C1.plain: In neither qubit type does the code reliably want a shorter readout than a single qubit does.
deviations: E12 (a): the ion parts are also reported with interiorBelowTauPhysResolved (the whole interval below τ*_phys), decided after seeing the A48 data; the automated verdict uses the pre-registered point flag.
E14 (b): shiftDelta, pL(τ_ref) − pL(τ_short) with a paired cluster interval, is a post-hoc addition reported beside the pre-registered rule.
E14 (d): the superconducting part uses the dense grid (27 points); on the standard grid (A49) d = 3 held in both bases.
E12: a τ*_log with fractionTied ≥ 0.5 is UNRESOLVED and enters no verdict.

C2.statement: Soft decoding is at or below hard at every τ, with most gain where readouts are short
C2.note: Learned decoder, soft above hard beyond the intervals (Wilson / cluster / paired cluster): Z trapped-ion 0 / 0 / 0 of 39; Z superconducting 0 / 0 / 0 of 81; X trapped-ion 0 / 0 / 0 of 39; X superconducting 0 / 0 / 0 of 81. Soft below hard beyond the paired interval: Z trapped-ion 13; Z superconducting 31; X trapped-ion 15; X superconducting 35, most at short τ. The verdict uses the pre-registered Wilson rule; the paired count agrees.
C2.plain: Weighing each readout by its confidence never hurt with the learned decoder, and helped most for short readouts.

C3.statement: Neither readout model dominates: along the τ grids the ion arm has lower error per round and the superconducting arm more rounds per second
C3.note: The outcome is fixed by construction: cycle times differ by about 3800x at d = 3 and gate noise is shared, so with these cards the superconducting arm always has more rounds per second and the ion arm a lower error per round. Shown as a trade-off, not as a finding. At τ*_log (d = 3, hard, learned): ion 0.00112 [0.000928, 0.00135] per round at 253 rounds/s; superconducting 0.00221 [0.00193, 0.00253] at 9.58e+5 rounds/s; neither dominates.
C3.plain: The ion makes fewer errors per round, the superconducting qubit more rounds per second; our parameters guaranteed this.
deviations: E12 (c): reported with informative: false; the U4 rule itself is unchanged.

C4.statement: Break-even ε̄ (d = 5 beats d = 3) similar on both arms, on the empirical ε̄ axis
C4.note: Empirical assignment-error axis, learned: hard: ion 0.237, superconducting no crossing (d = 5 below d = 3 at every grid point): undetermined; soft: ion no crossing (d = 5 below d = 3 at every grid point), superconducting no crossing (d = 5 below d = 3 at every grid point): undetermined. Wilson-based break-even intervals.
C4.plain: Undecided: on the superconducting qubit, distance 5 beat distance 3 at every readout quality tried, leaving nothing to compare.

C5.statement: The learned detector error model lowers the logical error against the naive one at every (d, arm, mode) at τ*_log, out of sample
C5.note: Out of sample at 4 rows (Z trapped-ion d3 hard, Z trapped-ion d3 soft, Z trapped-ion d5 hard, Z trapped-ion d5 soft; holdout.json -> setting2, rates learned from the original banks only). In sample at 11 rows (the X basis and the superconducting arm have no held-out banks). V18 (holdout.json -> setting1, flat ε = 0.02, hard): pass. Learned above naive beyond the Wilson intervals at 0 of 15 resolved rows; below beyond them at 13 (3 of them out of sample). Equal within the intervals at Z trapped-ion d3 hard, X trapped-ion d3 hard, so "lowers at every (d, arm, mode)" is met only in the sense that learned is never higher. 9 rows have an UNRESOLVED τ*_log and are excluded.
C5.plain: Learning the noise from the data never made decoding worse, and usually made it clearly better.
deviations: Out of sample only where held-out banks exist (DECISIONS E11): trapped ion, Z basis, d = 3 and 5; the other rows decode the banks the rates were learned from and carry inSample: true.

C6.statement: In the phase-flip memory the superconducting τ*_log is shorter than in the bit-flip memory when T2 < T1
C6.note: Not applicable with the card: the statement is conditional on T2 < T1, and the card has T2 = 77 µs ≥ T1 = 50 µs (DECISIONS E7, E12 (b)). Variant card T2 = 25 µs (UNSOURCED, illustrative; stage3_sc_x_T2_25.json against stage3_sc_dense.json, learned): d3 hard: X 0.691 [0.640, 0.792] µs against Z 0.710 [0.662, 0.990] µs; d3 soft: X 0.644 [0.548, 0.728] µs against Z 0.694 [0.563, 0.912] µs; d5 hard: X 0.798 [0.596, 0.810] µs against Z 0.942 [0.643, 0.977] µs; d5 soft: X 0.603 [0.561, 0.805] µs against Z 0.844 [0.518, 0.983] µs. The rule gives "undetermined": X is shorter in every point estimate, but the intervals overlap. pL(X) − pL(Z) at the grid point nearest the Z τ*_log (unpaired, different banks; cluster half-widths in quadrature): d3 hard +0.00300 [0.000983, 0.00500] at 0.7 µs; d3 soft +0.00263 [0.000633, 0.00476] at 0.7 µs; d5 hard +0.00103 [0.000427, 0.00163] at 0.95 µs; d5 soft +0.000219 [-0.000444, 0.000816] at 0.85 µs.
C6.plain: Does not apply: our superconducting qubit loses phase more slowly than energy. An invented faster-dephasing qubit leans yes, unresolved.
deviations: E14 (c): the variant card T2 = 25 µs is UNSOURCED (illustrative) and post hoc, chosen only to meet the premise T2 < T1.

CC-A22 asked for pairedClusterDiff of pL at matching τ; the X and Z files decode different banks (repx_* against rep_*) and per-shot failure counts are not stored, so the difference is unpaired, with the cluster half-widths combined in quadrature.

O4.statement: Ratio of bulk detector rates, X-basis to Z-basis banks, per (d, r): how biased forte-1 noise looks to the decoder (measurement, no hypothesis)
O4.note: Measurement, no hypothesis (no verdict). X over Z bulk detector rate (dem_forte1.json -> ratioXoverZ): d3 r1 1.041 [0.894, 1.213]; d3 r3 1.027 [0.959, 1.100]; d5 r3 1.000 [0.953, 1.048]; d5 r5 1.029 [0.995, 1.064]; d7 r3 1.021 [0.983, 1.061]; 5 of 5 intervals contain 1 (DECISIONS E5).
O4.plain: Measured, not tested: IonQ’s simulated gate noise looks the same to the decoder for bit flips and phase flips.

findings.statement: Post hoc, not pre-registered: on the trapped-ion arm, soft decoding is worse than hard beyond the intervals with the naive decoder and never with the learned decoder; the v1 C2 loss was a decoder-model artefact (the naive graph lacks the diagonal edges).
findings.source: holdout.json -> setting2 (out of sample); stage2_ion_v2b.json, stage2_ion_x_v2b.json (in sample)
findings.plain: Readout confidence seemed to hurt the ion only because the first decoder ignored a common error; fresh data confirm it.

sensitivity.skipped: not run: createScReadout: T2_us = 77 exceeds 2 * T1_us = 50

sensitivityNote: Six rows (three parameters, each x0.5 and x2) at full statistics: every shot, R = 2 readout draws, learned decoder, cluster intervals; τ*_log is the grid minimum (no bootstrap). Only the arm that owns the parameter is rerun; the other arm keeps its baseline value. pairedVsBaseline is the paired cluster difference of pL (d = 3, hard) against the baseline at the baseline τ*_log, on the same shots and seeds.

sensitivityBaseline.note: card values at the same statistics and seeds as the sensitivity rows (R = 2, all shots, learned); compare rows with this baseline, not with the headline tables (R = 4)

two_qubit_gate_us.source: IonQ Forte 1, 2-q gate speed 970 us (ZZ gate) at job submission: Robertson et al., 'Variational Gibbs State Preparation on Trapped-Ion Devices', arXiv:2603.03801 (2026), Table 1. For comparison: Aria two-qubit gate 600 us (Microsoft Azure Quantum IonQ provider page, Aria system timing); Forte Enterprise 1 650 us (same Table 1)

gate_layers_per_round.source: conservative choice: the 2(d-1) CNOTs of a round run one after another on the single chain (no published statement found that IonQ Forte runs two-qubit gates on disjoint pairs in parallel; simultaneous entangling gates in one chain are demonstrated only in research systems). See DECISIONS E8

reset_us.source: IonQ Forte 1, reset speed 50 us at job submission: Robertson et al., arXiv:2603.03801 (2026), Table 1 (Aria 1: 20 us; Forte Enterprise 1: 150 us, same table)

two_qubit_gate_us.source: Google Quantum AI, 'Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold', Nature 638, 920 (2025), arXiv:2408.13687, Supplementary Information Section I: CZ gates in 42 ns on the 105-qubit processor (37 ns on the 72-qubit processor)

gate_layers_per_round.source: derived: each round is two parallel CNOT layers

reset_us.source: multi-level reset to the ground state, total duration about 250 ns (error about 1e-3): McEwen et al., 'Removing leakage-induced correlated errors in superconducting quantum error correction', Nat. Commun. 12, 1761 (2021), arXiv:2102.06131, main text (Fig. 2 discussion: 'The total duration of the reset protocol is about 250 ns'; checked against the arXiv PDF Sat 10 Oct). Google's 1.1 us surface-code cycle (arXiv:2408.13687) gives no reset duration

R_bright_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), 171Yb+ with SNSPD, Results (Fig. 2a discussion): overall photon detection rate 472(14) kcps = 0.472 counts/us (collected, system efficiency 4.356%)

R_dark_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), Results and Methods: background count rate 4.2(1) cps = 4.2e-6 counts/us

gamma_bright_to_dark_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), Results (Fig. 2a discussion): dark pumping rate 341(13) Hz = 3.41e-4 /us

gamma_dark_to_bright_per_us.source: Crain et al., Commun. Phys. 2, 97 (2019), Results (Fig. 2a discussion): bright pumping rate 16.4(5) Hz = 1.64e-5 /us

T1_idle_us.source: Microsoft Azure Quantum IonQ provider documentation (learn.microsoft.com/azure/quantum/provider-ionq), IonQ Aria, System timing: T1 10-100 s (same 171Yb+ qubit as Forte; no Forte T1 is published there); lower end 10 s = 1e7 us used (conservative)

T2_idle_us.source: Microsoft Azure Quantum IonQ provider documentation (learn.microsoft.com/azure/quantum/provider-ionq), IonQ Aria, System timing: T2 1 s (same 171Yb+ qubit as Forte; no Forte T2 is published there) = 1e6 us; satisfies T2 <= 2 T1

crosstalk_rate_per_us.source: Gaebler et al., arXiv:2108.10932 (2021), Honeywell H0, 171Yb+, Table 2: probe-qubit average error with an interleaved dark measurement of a qubit 110 um away, minus the control: 1.3e-3 - 0.31e-3 = 1.0e-3 per 120 us detection (zone 2, micromotion hiding at 2.3 um on); converted with 1/2 (1 - exp(-Gamma tau)) = 1.0e-3 at tau = 120 us: Gamma = -ln(1 - 2e-3) / 120 us = 1.67e-5 /us. Lower bound for a same-species chain: unshielded and a few um apart, neighbours see more (the scan covers up to 1e-3 /us)

crosstalk_scan_per_us.source: scan grid spanning shielded to unshielded same-species chains; illustrative

tau_grid_us.source: spans the published detection-time range: 10.5-181.6 us (Noek et al., Opt. Lett. 38, 4735 (2013)), 11 us average and 500 us fixed window (Crain et al. 2019); 1-7 us added to resolve the short-time, photon-starved regime

chi_over_2pi_MHz.source: representative transmon value (plan section 7.4 default), not one device; published dispersive shifts span ~0.5-8 MHz, e.g. |chi|/2pi = 7.9 MHz in Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017), arXiv:1701.06933

kappa_over_2pi_MHz.source: chosen as kappa = 2 chi, the optimum of kappa |delta alpha|^2 at fixed nbar (plan section 7); Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017) use the same design rule with a Purcell filter, kappa_eff/2pi = 37.5 MHz

nbar.source: UNSOURCED (illustrative): a few photons, below typical critical photon numbers; plan section 7.4 default

eta.source: representative heterodyne chain with a quantum-limited amplifier (plan section 7.4 default); Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017) report eta = 0.66 with a phase-sensitive parametric amplifier, so 0.3 is conservative

T1_us.source: representative transmon T1 (plan section 7.4 default), within the published range from 7.6 us (Walter et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 7, 054020 (2017)) to a few hundred us in current devices

T2_us.source: Norris et al., arXiv:2503.12603 (2025), Sec. 3, device A qubit 2: median T1 = 50 us (matches T1_us) and median Hahn-echo T2 = 77 us over 104 measurements (Ramsey T2* = 50 us); echo value used for an idle with refocusing; satisfies T2 <= 2 T1 = 100 us

tau_grid_us.source: spans published integration times: 48-88 ns (Walter et al. 2017) up to the few-us regime where T1 decay dominates

definitions.cycleTime: layers * two_qubit_gate_us + tau + reset_us; layers = gate_layers_per_round (a number, or "2*(d-1)" evaluated at d: sequential ion gates, DECISIONS E8)
definitions.tradeoff: per d and mode, at every grid tau: roundsPerSecond and perRound = 0.5 (1 - (1 - 2 pL)^(1/r)); lo/hi are perRound of the Wilson bounds, loCluster/hiCluster of the cluster bounds
definitions.perRound: 0.5 (1 - (1 - 2 pL)^(1/r)) at tau*_log; pL and its bounds interpolated linearly in ln tau between grid points (the best grid point when tau*_log is at the grid edge)
definitions.perMicrosecond: perRound / cycleTime at tau*_log and d
definitions.intervals: lo/hi: Wilson 95% through the transform; loCluster/hiCluster: cluster bootstrap over quantum shots (B = 500, CC-A19) through the same transform. Cluster intervals are the honest ones where gate faults dominate; Wilson is kept beside them
definitions.budgetAtOptimum: Stage 2/3 budget arrays interpolated in ln tau at tau*_log (d = 3, hard, learned); gate is the mean of the learned edge classes
definitions.breakEven: first sign change of pL(d=5) - pL(d=3) in tau order, x axis averageAssignmentError() (belief; empiricalAxis: the F1 empirical curve); interval from the crossings of hi5 - lo3 and lo5 - hi3 (Wilson) on the same grid segment
definitions.conclusions: C1-C6 and O4 follow team checklist Section 1.2 (statements verbatim) with the rules in tools/sweep.mjs (c1Conclusion ... o4Conclusion); verdict equals automated unless the note gives Person A's different reading; informative and deviations per U4 revision 2.1; plain is a draft edited at A55
definitions.tieRule: a tau*_log with fractionTied >= 0.5 is UNRESOLVED and enters no verdict (DECISIONS E12)

sensitivity.shots: all shots of the Z-basis rep_* banks

provenance.sensitivitySeedRule: seed = 4000000 + (superconducting ? 100000 : 0) + 10000*d + 1000*logical + 10*tauIndex + draw (baseline and every scaled run; hard and soft share it); cluster seeds 4600000 (ion), 4700000 (superconducting) + 10000*d + 1000*modeIndex + tauIndex; pairedVsBaseline + 900000 + tauIndex
